findings.what: The palette-size error message changed from "a palette needs 2 to 256 colours, got N" to "a palette needs 2-256 colours, got N". The text now differs from lattice_core/palette.py:37/121 and palettes/io.py:62/149, which still say "2 to 256".
findings.why: This message belongs to the shipped dithering app and users can see it. The wording changed only to fit the 400-line budget, so the core now words the same error two ways. The error type is still ValueError and no test matches this text, so it is not a blocker.
findings.fix: Put back the "{MIN} to {MAX} colours" wording in _rows_to_palette.

findings.what: The _validate_order and _palette_for(extracted) refactors change which error is reported first. For example, order [0, 0, 5] used to report "repeated" and now reports "outside". An invalid locked hex is now reported before an out-of-range extract_k.
findings.why: Both are refactors of frozen behaviour outside the card's spec, made only to save lines. Every input is still rejected with the same error type, so this is not an E6, but the frozen code changed for no functional reason.
findings.fix: Either restore the HEAD bodies and save lines elsewhere, or record the reordering in DEVIATIONS.

findings.what: RenderStyle stores the decoded JSON as a plain dict. Anyone holding the style can still run style.options[k] = object() after construction.
findings.why: The caller-dict hole required by the card is closed, but invariant 6 can still be broken by mutating the field directly.

findings.what: The order of sub-points inside subindex[..., k] and the default stencil (row-major, k = r*sx + c) is not documented. Values from sample_points() are not checked to be finite or to lie in [0, 1]; NaN goes through astype(int64).
findings.why: The braille and sextant cards will pack bits based on this order, so it must be stated. A NaN stencil gives undefined indices instead of a typed error.
findings.fix: State the row-major ordering in the _subindex and _stencil_points docstrings. Reject non-finite points or points outside [0, 1] with a ValueError.

findings.what: The fn parameter of _run and _subindex has no type annotation. render_with_palette silently ignores the palette argument in continuous mode.
findings.why: Hygiene; the ignored palette could surprise a caller.
findings.fix: Annotate fn as Callable[[Image, Palette, dict], np.ndarray]. Document or reject a palette passed in continuous mode.

regression: none. The pixel path stays bit-identical: color.downscale already edge-pads, so the new _pad_to_cells → downscale step equals the 1.0 path, and the witnesses on 20 images × 5 palettes × non-divisible sizes are green. The geometry change from half-to-even to floor(x+0.5) is asked for by the card (DEV-205). The only other changes are palette error text and error precedence (see minors).
renderer_invariants: all six hold. Inv. 1: the render_frame shape is now checked, and the crop to target still applies. Inv. 2/3: the pipeline does not mutate grid or palette, and it holds no module state. Inv. 4: the H11 rule keeps the source aspect (a=2.0 gives 4×2, a=0.5 gives 2×4). Inv. 5: untouched. Inv. 6: the options copy is stored (mutable field, minor).
tests_that_cannot_fail: test_no_subindex_when_subgrid_is_one (passes on HEAD: subindex defaults to None; acceptable as a guard)
test_default_stencil_is_the_cell_mean_luma_for_a_pixel_renderer (passes on HEAD by design: a preservation test, not new behaviour)
test_continuous_mode_calls_no_renderer_and_builds_no_grid: the CellGrid spy is redundant because the forbid stub already raises; it still fails if the code path is reached
notes:
The two blockers and four majors from pass 1 are fixed and checked against the diff. The stencil now includes the cell origin and is clamped. Sub-points are area-averaged on the padded step-5 image and dithered at (rows·sy, cols·sx). The pack/transposition order matches the meshgrid stencil order. The monotonicity test is meaningful.
Continuous mode follows the H11 reformulation in the card (steps 6-11 skipped), not the S1 text of the 0.1.0-draft excerpt; this is expected.
Default stencil for subgrid (1,1) = cell mean (k=1). Renderers with k>1 and subgrid (1,1), such as glyph_shape k=6, must implement sample_points(); L-cards should state this.
No abstraction leak and no host coupling in the diff. I did not re-run pytest locally (approval refused); I relied on the orchestrator's G2 result (1336 passed).
